bihar_raw_news.title: NTPC and NPCIL to invest 1.4 lakh cr in Bihar nuclear plants - The Economic Times
bihar_raw_news.content: iStock NEW DELHI: State-owned NTPC Ltd and Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd ( NPCIL ) have signed agreements to set up two nuclear power plants of 2,800 MW each in Bihar, involving a combined investment of Rs 1.4 lakh crore. The agreements are part of six energy projects worth Rs 1,72,885 crore for which memoranda of understanding were exchanged on Friday. The projects comprise two nuclear power plants and four pumped storage facilities, with a combined power generation capacity of 11,600 MW and energy storage capacity of 36,078 MWh. NTPC plans to set up a 2,800 MW nuclear power plant at Bhitiya in Banka district at an estimated cost of Rs 70,000 crore. NPCIL will develop another 2,800 MW plant at Talhar in Siwan district, also at a cost of Rs 70,000 crore. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.title: “My father would be overjoyed”: Chirag Paswan on PM Modi dedicating Nitish Setu to Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: “My father would be overjoyed”: Chirag Paswan on PM Modi dedicating Nitish Setu to Bihar ANI | Updated: Nov 21, 2026 03:09 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], November 21 (ANI): Union Minister Chirag Paswan on Friday expressed happiness over the inauguration of Nitish Setu in Bihar, saying the bridge fulfilled a long-standing demand of the people of the region and that his late father, Ram Vilas Paswan, would have been overjoyed to see the dream realised. Reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Bihar and the inauguration of the bridge, Chirag Paswan said it was a momentous occasion for him as the Prime Minister's visit to his Lok Sabha constituency brought a significant gift for the people of the region. "This is a momentous occasion for me. The Prime Minister’s visit to my Lok Sabha constituency brings a significant gift to the people of this region: the Nitish Setu (bridge)," he said. He further said that the project was a long-standing demand of residents and recalled the efforts made by his late father towards its realisation. "This project was a long-standing demand of the residents, one for which my leader and my father, the late Ram Vilas Paswan, had worked tirelessly. As this dream is realised today, I am certain that my father, wherever he may be, would be overjoyed to see this long-held aspiration of the people being fulfilled," he added. Meanwhile, BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was dedicated to the development of Bihar and that several development projects were being inaugurated and dedicated to the nation. "The Prime Minister is dedicated to the development of Bihar. As we reach the one-year mark, the 'Nitish Setu' (bridge) will be inaugurated, along with several other development projects. The Prime Minister has been committed to Bihar’s progress from the very beginning, which is a matter of pride for the people of Bihar," he said. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Bihar on Saturday, during which he will visit Nitish Setu in Vaishali district. He will thereafter inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects and lay the foundation stone of several projects worth around Rs 34,470 crore. According to an official release, the projects span road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, water resources, education, healthcare, transport and other key sectors, and are aimed at strengthening infrastructure and improving public services across the state. The Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation Nitish Setu, an extradosed cable-stayed bridge over the River Ganga, constructed at a cost of around Rs 4,280 crore. The 19.7-km-long project connects Kachhi Dargah on NH-22 in Patna district with Bidupur on NH-322 in Vaishali district. It comprises a 9.7-km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads. The bridge will provide an additional crossing over the River Ganga, easing traffic pressure on the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu and reducing travel time between North and South Bihar. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted that 21st-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity. Digital platforms have made knowledge sharing, cultural exchange and international collaboration easier than ever before and SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities. Inaugurating the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi today, the Prime Minister said that the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) has completed 25 years since its establishment and over the years, the SCO has significantly expanded cooperation in the areas of security, economy and connectivity. He said, in this context, cultural and civilizational cooperation will further strengthen relations among member countries. The Prime Minister expressed confidence that the forum will generate new ideas, create fresh opportunities for cultural cooperation, and enable shared civilizational experiences to play an important role in bringing the world together as cultural connections are the strongest guarantee of global peace, The Prime Minister noted that 21st-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity. Mr Modi highlighted that digital platforms have made knowledge sharing, cultural exchange and international collaboration easier than ever before and SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities. The Prime Minister said, the Museums, Libraries and Archives in the countries preserve a priceless heritage spanning thousands of years and today technology offers excellent opportunities to bring this heritage to the new generation. He suggested that countries can collaborate on the Digitisation and Translation of ancient texts and through Joint Research Projects, new aspects of shared history can be broguht to the fore. He said, this will enable a young person anywhere in the world to understand another country’s Cultural Heritage much better. The Prime Minister said that Indian culture has taught ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam which means the whole world is its family and therefore, the wish of India for its own well-being is deeply rooted in the spirit of global well-being. He said, India considers mutual harmony the foundation of global well-being. Noting that Empires have certainly changed the map of the world, but civilisational dialogues have changed the way the world’s thinking and has enriched it. Mr Modi said, the SCO civilisational summit is not merely a ceremonial platform, as it can become a platform for giving the world direction. Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister for Culture and Tourism, Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that over the past twenty-five years of its journey, the SCO has emerged into an important platform for mutual trust, co-operation and shared progress. He said, history reminds that civilisations flourish not in isolation, but through dialogue and mutual enrichment. Mr Shekhawat said, this profound inheritance inspired Prime Minister Modi to propose the SCO Civilization Dialogue Forum at the Tianjin Summit in 2025. This initiative reflects India’s timeless civilizational philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam-the world is one family. He described it a philosophy that finds a natural resonance in the Shanghai Spirit of mutual respect, equality and shared development. The three day SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum which is being held till 22nd of this month aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of the region, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation. Prime Minister Modi also also undertook a walkthrough of the exhibitions showcasing India’s archaeological, artistic and literary heritage titled “ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence.It offers an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE, including excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries. The “Mahabharat Scroll Pavilion – Anant: A Rare 18th Century Mahabharata Scroll” will showcase an illustrated scroll reflecting India’s rich epic and artistic traditions.

national_raw_news.title: Govt sanctions 1.75 lakh houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0
national_raw_news.content: The Government has sanctioned 1.75 lakh houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) during the 11th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee held under the chairmanship of Secretary, Department of Urban Development, Satendra Singh. An additional in-principle approval for 1.5 lakh houses was also sanctioned during the meeting held yesterday. During the meeting, the Secretary directed States and Union Territories to accelerate expenditure and ensure optimal utilisation of sanctioned funds, along with ensuring timely release of funds to beneficiaries and implementing agencies for seamless implementation of scheme. He further mentioned about strengthening monitoring, geo-tagging of houses and complete verification of all pending applications within stipulated timelines. Furthermore, in-principle approval has been given for over 1.27 lakh houses in Andhra Pradesh and to over 22,000 houses in Maharashtra, subject to submission of necessary compliance and adherence to Scheme Guidelines by the respective States. With these approvals, the total count of houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0 has crossed 24 lakhs. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs said that the latest approval marks another significant step towards expanding access to pucca houses for eligible urban families, particularly those belonging to the Economically Weaker Section. PMAY-U 2.0, launched in September 2024, aims to support one crore additional eligible EWS, Low Income Group and Middle Income Group families in constructing or purchasing pucca houses through different verticals.

national_raw_news.title: 57th IFFI opens in Goa to celebrate diverse cinema and storytelling traditions from across the world
national_raw_news.content: The 57th International Film Festival of India, IFFI, opened in Goa today with a spectacular opening ceremony, bringing together filmmakers, actors, cinema enthusiasts and delegates from India and across the world. The opening ceremony was graced by Actors Karthik Aryan and Sai Pallavi. Three-time Grammy Award-winning composer Ricky Kej presented a special symphonic orchestra performance titled ‘A World of Cinema Through Music’, bringing together the magic of music and the universal language of cinema. This year’s festival, centred on the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, promises nine days of international cinema, creative exchange and opportunities for emerging filmmakers. Chief Minister Dr Pramod Sawant welcomed national and international delegates and said Goa has made extensive preparations to ensure an enhanced festival experience this year. He said IFFI provides an additional boost to tourism and offers an important platform for regional cinema, particularly Konkani and Marathi films. He also reiterated the state’s commitment to developing permanent infrastructure to strengthen Goa’s position as an international film festival destination. Addressing the opening ceremony, Festival Director and acclaimed filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker said cinema has the power to transcend geographical, linguistic and cultural boundaries and connect people through shared human emotions. The opening ceremony also highlighted the growing opportunities for young filmmakers through the WAVES Film Bazaar, which connects aspiring writers, directors and producers with investors, distributors and international collaborators. NFDC Chairman G. Krishnakumar described the Film Bazaar as an important platform that has transformed opportunities for aspiring filmmakers by bringing creative talent and potential investors under one roof. Poland, this year’s Country of Focus, received special attention with the festival opening with the Indian premiere of Fatherland, directed by Oscar-winning filmmaker Pawel Pawlikowski. The black-and-white drama explores history, family relationships and the complexities of a divided homeland through the story of Nobel Prize-winning German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika. Polish Ambassador to India appreciated the organisers for selecting Poland as the Country of Focus and choosing Fatherland as the opening film. He said the film’s exploration of borders, morality, history and personal relationships closely reflects this year’s festival theme. Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Chanchal Kumar said this year’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, reflects the extraordinary ability of films to connect audiences across borders through shared stories and human experiences. Mr. Kumar said IFFI is more than a gathering of films, as it brings together cultures, ideas, memories and experiences. He added that cinema gives timeless ideas a contemporary expression. He also highlighted that this year’s festival features 52 films directed by women and 62 films by debut filmmakers, reflecting the growing diversity of voices shaping the future of cinema. Earlier in the day, Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker unveiled the official brochure and outlined the festival’s vision during a media briefing. In another significant initiative, the National Film Development Corporation has partnered with Svayam to make IFFI more accessible and inclusive for persons with disabilities and reduced mobility. Accessibility audits, volunteer sensitisation workshops and an Accessibility Simulation Zone are among the measures planned across festival venues. With cinema from across continents, a special focus on emerging talent and a strong emphasis on inclusivity, the 57th IFFI has begun its nine-day journey in Goa, inviting audiences to discover stories that go beyond borders.

national_raw_news.title: Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya highlights India’s sporting ecosystem over past 12 years 8 hours ago 130
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, said that schemes like Khelo India Mission, Fit India Movement and Target Olympic Podium Scheme are helping expand grassroots participation, identify sporting talent and create pathways for high-performance sports. Addressing the 16th edition of FICCI’s Global Summit on the Business of Sports TURF-2026 today in New Delhi, the Minister highlighted the transformation of India’s sporting ecosystem over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr Mandaviya further said that the vision is to transform India from a sporting nation into a global sports ecosystem. He invited international partners, innovators, manufacturers, and sporting institutions to become part of this transformation. The minister also highlighted the government’s focus on strengthening sports infrastructure and manufacturing capabilities. He said the government has approved a sports goods manufacturing scheme with an outlay of nearly two thousand crore rupees to make India a global hub for sports goods manufacturing and innovation. Calling for greater private sector participation, Mr Mandaviya encouraged industry leaders to invest in sports infrastructure, high-performance academies, sports science facilities, technology and athlete management systems. He further highlighted India’s preparations for the Commonwealth Games 2030 and its ambition to host the 2036 Olympic Games. France is the partner country for this year’s summit, with an MoU signed to strengthen India-France cooperation in the sports sector.

national_raw_news.title: Govt to build Street Food Hubs at Tangmarg and Lakhanpur to promote local tourism and livelihood 3 hours ago 72
national_raw_news.content: In a significant initiative to strengthen local livelihoods, promote tourism and improve public amenities, the Jammu and Kashmir Government has accorded administrative approval for the construction of two Street Food Hubs at Tangmarg and Lakhanpur at a combined cost of Rs. 9.85 crore. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the projects assume special significance in view of the strategic and tourism importance of the two locations. Lakhanpur, the gateway to Jammu and Kashmir and J&K’s first town for visitors entering from Punjab, serves as the first point of entry for a large number of tourists, pilgrims and travellers. Similarly, Tangmarg is the first major tourist destination on the route to the world-famous ski resort of Gulmarg, welcoming visitors heading towards the popular tourist resort. The projects include construction of a Street Food Hub at Tangmarg at an approved cost of Rs. 3.81 crore and a Clean Street Food Hub at Lakhanpur at a cost of Rs. 6.04 crore. The funding will be provided under PM SVANidhi and the Capex Budget (MRDA Sector). The initiative aims to provide organised, hygienic and well-equipped spaces for street vendors, improve public amenities and ensure access to safe and quality food for residents, tourists and other visitors. The development of these facilities is expected to enhance the overall visitor experience at two important entry and tourism points of J&K, while providing better livelihood opportunities to street vendors and giving a boost to local economic activity.

national_raw_news.title: 57th International Film Festival of India to begin today in Goa with grand opening ceremony
national_raw_news.content: The 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India, IFFI 2026, begins today with a grand opening ceremony in the evening. Chief Minister Pramod Sawant and festival director, filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker will be inaugurating the nine-day cinematic extravaganza that would see cinema lovers, filmmakers, artists and actors coming together to celebrate the magic of cinema. The theme for this year’s edition, ‘Stories Without Borders’, befits the spirit of the festival that will see an array of cinematic stories converge on the shores of Goa. The opening Film ‘Fatherland’ directed by Pawel Pawlikoski will be screened today across all the venues of the festival. Akashvani correspondents reported that Goa is decked up with vibrant lights and decorations, in line with the theme of the festival, ‘Stories Without Borders’. Featuring over 150 international films from 86 countries, IFFI 2026 promises a diverse cinematic experience, showcasing compelling narratives, emerging talent and acclaimed filmmakers. The festival will also provide a platform for meaningful conversations, masterclasses, industry interactions and discussions on the evolving landscape of world cinema. Among the major highlights are the opening film, Fatherland, by Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski, and the closing film, We Are All Strangers, by Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen. With special sections on animation and films about filmmaking, alongside masterclasses, workshops, competitions and the WAVES Film Bazaar, IFFI 2026 aims to strengthen India’s engagement with the global film industry while celebrating the diversity and transformative power of cinema. IFFI 2026 promises to be not just a celebration of films but also a meeting ground for cultures, creative ideas and stories that transcend geographical and linguistic boundaries.

national_raw_news.title: Women’s hockey: India defeat Malaysia 4-1 19 Nov 2026 | 6:47 PM 338
national_raw_news.content: The Indian women’s hockey team defeated Malaysia 4-1 in the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy being held in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Khan Mumtaz, captain Salima Tete, Pooja Sahu and Lalremsiami scored one goal each for India. Nuramirah Zulkifli scored the only goal for Malaysia. Earlier in the day, China defeated Thailand 7-0 in the opening match. Feng Qiagmiao and Deng Qiuchan scored two goals each for China, while three other players scored one goal each. In the second match of the day, Japan defeated South Korea 1-0. The match remained goalless until the final minutes. In the 59th minute, Saito Hanami scored from a penalty corner to give Japan the win. Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav inaugurated the tournament today. The stadium was lit up with a grand fireworks display, and a large number of spectators came to watch the matches. Six countries, including India, are taking part in the tournament. The tournament is being held at the International Sports Complex in Barkheda Nathu, Bhopal, from November 19 to 28. Entry to the stadium is free for spectators. On Saturday, China will play Malaysia at 2:30 PM, Thailand will face Japan at 4:45 PM, and hosts India will take on South Korea at 7 PM.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister Piyush Goyal urges Indian businesses to utilise opportunities opened by recent FTAs 4 hours ago 49
national_raw_news.content: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has urged Indian businesses to utilise opportunities opened by recent free trade agreements(FTAs). Addressing the valedictory session of FICCI’s Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said, India’s preferential access to global markets has expanded by an additional 60 trillion dollars over the last four-and-a-half years, taking the total to approximately 70 trillion dollars. Referring to his recent visits to Egypt and Italy, the Minister said that the growing interest of international partners in working with India reflects the country’s increasing global standing. He noted that discussions have been initiated to explore a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement with Egypt, while the forthcoming India-EU FTA has generated considerable interest among Italian businesses. He said that the commitment of international businesses to work with India reflects the growing opportunities for trade, investment and industrial cooperation. Highlighting the country’s growing economic strength and global engagement, Mr Goyal said that India has set a target of achieving 1 trillion dollars in exports in Financial Year 2026-27. He noted that the country recorded exports of 480 billion dollars in the first six months of the current financial year. The Minister spoke about India’s transformation over the past decade, noting improvements in infrastructure, digital connectivity, financial inclusion and the banking sector. He added that the country’s growing middle class, purchasing power and expanding domestic market provide a strong foundation for economic growth.

national_raw_news.title: UP govt decides to allocate 4.19 acres of govt land in Varanasi to strengthen security arrangements at Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham 2 hours ago 41
national_raw_news.content: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to allocate 4.19 acres of government land in Varanasi, on lease to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, to strengthen security arrangements at the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham. The decision aims to facilitate the permanent deployment of Central Armed Police Forces near the temple complex and ensure a swift response in emergency situations. The allocation will, however, remain subject to the final decision of the competent court. The land, measuring 1.697 hectares, is located in the Sadar tehsil of Varanasi, in villages Kila Kohna and Saretabad. According to the prevailing circle rate, its estimated market value is around 44.04 crore rupees. The land will be allotted free of cost for a maximum period of 90 years, through successive renewals of 30 years each, under the special provisions of the Government Property Management (Amendment) Rules, 2003. Following the redevelopment of the Kashi Vishwanath Dham, lakhs of devotees, tourists and distinguished visitors from India and abroad visit the temple every day. Considering the growing footfall and the sensitive nature of the area, the permanent deployment of central security forces is expected to further strengthen its multi-layered security arrangements. Under the terms of the lease, the land will remain non-transferable and can be used exclusively for the designated purpose of strengthening security. Ownership of the land will continue to vest with the Revenue Department of the Uttar Pradesh government. The lease deed will be executed by the District Magistrate of Varanasi on behalf of the Governor of Uttar Pradesh.

national_raw_news.title: India records $11.3 bn FPIs in first 18 days of November: CEA Anantha Nageswaran
national_raw_news.content: Chief Economic Adviser, Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran today said that foreign capital is returning sharply to India as oil prices cool below 100 dollars per barrel and the emerging risks regarding AI valuation. Addressing the 65th General Assembly and Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE) in Mumbai, Dr. Nageswaran said India has recorded foreign portfolio inflows of 11.3 billion dollars in just the first 18 days of November. The CEA further underlined that India remains poised to be a big beneficiary in the course of the next financial year as the AI bubble comes down to realistic levels, adding that earlier currency pressures from AI outflows will now likely turn into a source of currency strength. He also highlighted that India has sustained roughly 7 per cent real GDP growth despite global tariff turmoil, supply shocks, and geopolitical conflicts, adding that India has been successful in lifting roughly 500 million people above the 4.20 dollar-a-day moderate poverty line, with rural poverty falling faster than urban in the past decade. While noting that the Indian Government, which had been cautious about trade liberalisation until around 2020, Dr. Nageswaran said that the government has embraced free trade agreements with considerable enthusiasm in the post-pandemic period. He said that India has not only concluded but also operationalised trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand this year alone. He added that a trade agreement with the European Union has also been concluded while trade agreements with the US and Canada are also imminent. Pointing towards India’s strong export performance in the current financial year, the CEA said exports of goods and services stood at around 569 billion dollars from April to October, registering a growth of nearly 17 percent. Talking about the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the CEA flagged five unique challenges – geopolitical fragmentation, China’s manufacturing scale, the energy trilemma, AI-led job shifts, and social media’s impact on youth cognitive skills. To counter these, the CEA said closing technology gaps will buy resilience for India, while agriculture, trade skills, and human-centric services will buy leverage for India.

Top Stories of the Day Share DD India November 20, 2026 8:22 AM IST Prime Minister | SCO | Shanghai Cooperation Organisation | SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum | Narendra Modi | PM Modi PM Modi to inaugurate first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi on November 20 Author: DD India Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila in New Delhi on November 20, at around 5:30 PM. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The three-day Forum, scheduled from November 20 to 22, aims to celebrate the rich and interconnected civilisational heritage of SCO member countries, strengthen people-to-people ties and promote cross-cultural dialogue and cooperation. The initiative follows a proposal made by PM Modi at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025 to establish a dedicated platform for civilisational dialogue under the SCO framework. The proposal was subsequently welcomed in the Bishkek Declaration of the organisation. Cultural showcase to highlight India-Eurasia connections The inaugural ceremony will feature a cultural presentation titled “Civilisations in Conversation – Cultural Show”, combining music, dance, visual storytelling and narration. Based on the theme “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – The World Is One Family”, the presentation will highlight cultural connections between India and the wider Eurasian region. The Forum will also host exhibitions showcasing India’s archaeological, artistic and literary heritage under the title “ASTITVA – The Essence of Our Existence.” The exhibition will offer visitors an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence dating from 1200 BCE to 1200 CE. It will include excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries. Another key attraction will be the “Mahabharat Scroll Pavilion – Anant: A Rare 18th Century Mahabharata Scroll”, featuring an illustrated scroll that reflects India’s rich epic and artistic traditions. Four thematic sessions to explore shared civilisational heritage Four thematic sessions will be organised on November 21 and 22, bringing together scholars, academics, subject experts and cultural representatives from across the SCO region. The discussions will explore a range of shared cultural and intellectual traditions, including music and performing arts, textiles, cuisine and traditional games. Participants will also examine common traditions in art and architecture, as well as language and literary heritage, including scripts and manuscripts. Monastic trails and philosophical traditions will form another key area of discussion. national_raw_news.content: Srinagar to get Rs 361 cr waste processing facility at Achan Advertisment Breaking News Top Stories Srinagar to get Rs 361 cr waste processing facility at Achan RK News 20 Nov 2026 03:32 IST Follow Us 125-tonne construction waste plant targeted for Dec 91,789 tonnes of accumulated material processed at dumpsite Srinagar, Nov 19: In a major move to strengthen solid waste management in Srinagar, the Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC) has proposed an integrated waste processing facility with a capacity of 800 tonnes per day at Achan, involving an estimated investment of Rs 361 crore, while 91,789 tonnes of accumulated waste have already been processed at the dumpsite as part of efforts to reclaim the site and reduce environmental risks. Joint Commissioner, Srinagar Municipal Corporation, Syed Abul Qasim, disclosed these details during a press briefing organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, in collaboration with the Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee (JKPCC) on Thursday to discuss the implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026. Qasim said the proposed facility at Achan would include multiple waste processing components aimed at reducing dependence on conventional dumping and improving the recovery of reusable materials. The project, estimated to cost Rs 361 crore, will have facilities for material recovery, compressed biogas generation, composting and refuse-derived fuel processing. He said the integrated facility would enable the processing of different categories of municipal waste and support efforts to recover useful resources from waste generated across Srinagar. Highlighting the ongoing work at the Achan dumpsite near Anchar Lake, Qasim said approximately 91,789 tonnes of waste had already been processed as part of measures to reclaim the site and address environmental concerns associated with accumulated waste. The processing work, he said, is aimed at recovering useful materials, reducing the volume of accumulated waste and limiting environmental risks at the site. The Joint Commissioner also informed that a leachate treatment plant has been proposed at Achan to address environmental concerns arising from liquid waste generated at the dumping site. Leachate, the contaminated liquid that forms when water passes through accumulated waste, requires treatment to prevent potential pollution of surrounding soil and water resources. In another development, Qasim said a construction and demolition waste processing plant with a capacity of 125 tonnes per day is projected to be completed by December 2026. The facility is intended to strengthen the city's capacity to process waste generated from construction and demolition activities rather than allowing such material to accumulate at dumping locations. The proposed projects form part of SMC's efforts to improve waste processing infrastructure and address longstanding waste management challenges in the city. Meanwhile, Chairman JKPCC, Vasu Yadav, said the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, introduce stricter provisions for waste segregation, scientific processing and accountability among waste generators. He said the new framework requires segregation of waste at source into four categories — wet waste, dry waste, sanitary waste and special care waste. national_raw_news.title: J&K Cities face Waste Management test as new rules mandate four-way segregation
national_raw_news.content: J&K Cities face Waste Management test as new rules mandate four-way segregation – The Kashmir Horizon About Us Contact Us Our Team Advertise with Us Contributors FAQ Privacy Policy Terms of Service Friday, November 20, 2026 EPAPER HOME Region City News Srinagar Jammu News In Focus Opinion Editorial Ideas My Idea Friday Faith Letter to the Editor Business Sports India World Snapshots ePaper No Result View All Result HOME Region City News Srinagar Jammu News In Focus Opinion Editorial Ideas My Idea Friday Faith Letter to the Editor Business Sports India World Snapshots ePaper No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home Top News J&K Cities face Waste Management test as new rules mandate four-way segregation by Irfan Yattoo November 20, 2026 in Top News A A A A Reset Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Whatsapp Telegram Email • ₹361-crore integrated facility planned at Achan • JMC announces penalties for violations by bulk waste generators Srinagar| Nov, 19: With the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, placing greater emphasis on segregation at source, scientific processing and accountability, officials of the Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee (JKPCC) and municipal corporations on Wednesday outlined measures being taken to strengthen waste management in Jammu and Srinagar, while calling for greater public participation in their implementation. The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, in collaboration with JKPCC, organised a press briefing to explain the key provisions of the new Rules and sensitise media organisations and the public about the responsibilities of different stakeholders. The Rules place particular emphasis on segregation of waste at source into four categories—wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste. The framework also seeks to strengthen scientific waste processing, recycling, resource recovery and remediation of legacy dumpsites, while ensuring greater accountability among waste generators. JKPCC Chairman Vasu Yadav said the Rules provide for measures such as user fees, spot fines and environmental compensation to ensure compliance. He stressed that effective implementation would require coordinated action by government agencies, institutions, commercial establishments and citizens. Yadav said source segregation and scientific processing must become an integral part of waste management practices, adding that recycling and resource recovery were important for reducing the burden on disposal sites. In her opening remarks, Director PIB Jammu Neha Jalali said the press briefing was organised to familiarise media organisations and the public with the provisions of the Rules and promote awareness about responsible waste disposal. IFFI 26 Share DD India November 20, 2026 3:51 PM IST 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) | Stories Without Borders | IFFI 57 to Showcase Cinema Beyond Geographical ‘Stories Without Borders’: IFFI 57 to Showcase Cinema Beyond Geographical and Socio-Cultural Divides Author: DD India The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) will celebrate cinema that transcends geographical, social and cultural boundaries under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker said during a media briefing at the PIB Media Centre in Panaji, Goa. The briefing also attended by National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) Managing Director Dhiraj Singh and moderated by Smita Vats Sharma, Director General (West), Press Information Bureau (PIB). Outlining the vision for this year’s festival, Gowariker said the theme goes beyond territorial boundaries to explore divisions within families and societies, including those arising from caste, social differences and other socio-cultural realities. He said IFFI aims to bring together stories that transcend these divides and reflect shared human experiences across cultures. Highlighting the festival’s expanded programming, Gowariker announced the introduction of three new sections — Animation, Documentary and Films about Films. He stressed the growing importance of documentaries and the need to provide greater visibility and opportunities to documentary filmmakers. As part of this initiative, IFFI will host a special gala presentation featuring films by winners of the recently concluded Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF). Gowariker said the festival’s various sections, including retrospectives, curated showcases and special screenings, would offer audiences an opportunity to explore the diversity of cinema. He encouraged media professionals to look beyond their individual film preferences and attend gala screenings, red-carpet events, international press conferences and Panorama interactions. He noted that such engagements would allow filmmakers and visiting delegates to present their work while helping audiences discover different cinematic perspectives. Emphasising the media’s role in expanding the festival’s reach, Gowariker urged journalists to watch and cover films across various sections, including retrospectives, while maintaining their independent judgement and critical perspectives. He said media coverage was important in taking IFFI’s films and stories to audiences across the country. He also expressed willingness to facilitate informal interactions between the festival team and media representatives during the event. Taking into account journalists’ professional commitments, he said the scheduling of interactions had been adjusted to provide greater flexibility and sufficient time for festival coverage. During the briefing, Gowariker also unveiled the official brochure of the 57th IFFI. The interaction highlighted the festival’s vision and programming priorities, as well as the role of media engagement in strengthening IFFI as an international platform for cinema and cross-cultural exchange. -PIB Top Stories of the Day View All 27 minutes ago Vice President Radhakrishnan calls for responsible citizens... 54 minutes...

Excelsior Correspondent JAMMU, Nov 19: The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, and the Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee (JKPCC) today held a press briefing on the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, highlighting mandatory waste segregation, scientific processing, recycling and public participation for effective implementation of the new framework. Click here to watch video JKPCC Chairman Vasu Yadav outlined the key provisions of the rules, which mandate segregation of waste at source into four categories — wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste — besides emphasising scientific processing, resource recovery, recycling and remediation of legacy dumpsites. Yadav said the rules also provide for user charges, spot fines and environmental compensation to ensure compliance, calling for coordinated efforts by government agencies, institutions, commercial establishments and citizens in adopting responsible waste management practices. PIB Jammu Director Neha Jalali said the briefing was organised to familiarise media organisations and the public with the provisions of the new rules and promote responsible waste disposal. She stressed the need for behavioural change and active participation of citizens, institutions and local authorities, while underlining the role of media in spreading awareness about cleanliness and sustainable waste management. Jammu Municipal Corporation (JMC) Commissioner Ayushi Sudan said bulk waste generators are required to register through a dedicated online portal to facilitate monitoring and compliance with prescribed norms. She said dumping waste in public places by bulk waste generators attracts a penalty of Rs 10,000 per violation, besides user charges of Rs 5,000. She said the Corporation is also using GPS-enabled vehicles to monitor waste collection and has urged citizens to register sanitation-related complaints through the ‘My Jammu’ mobile application. Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC) Joint Commissioner Syed Abul Qasim said around 91,789 tonnes of waste had been processed at the Achan dumpsite near Anchar Lake. He said an 800-tonne-per-day integrated waste management facility, estimated to cost Rs 361 crore, is proposed at Achan, with provisions for material recovery, compressed biogas generation, composting and refuse-derived fuel processing. A leachate treatment plant is also proposed, while a 125-tonne-per-day construction and demolition waste processing facility is expected to be completed by December 2026, the SMC Joint Commissioner said. Sign In Prefer Prefer PM Modi (Pic Via PIB) Prime Minister Narendra Modi challenged corporate India yesterday (19 November) over whether businesses had increased employment and raised salaries following substantial tax concessions, putting the country's business leaders on the spot at a major industry gathering. Addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry's (FICCI) annual general meeting at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on 19 November, PM Modi questioned whether companies had delivered enough in return for government tax relief. The Prime Minister pointed out that the government had reduced the basic corporate tax rate from 30 per cent to 22 per cent, whilst also providing income tax relief to individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh annually. PM Modi directly asked business leaders: "Did you hire more employees? Did you increase their salaries?" The remarks drew attention to whether corporate tax concessions had delivered tangible benefits for workers through expanded recruitment and improved wages. PM Modi urged companies to evaluate their contribution to employment generation and investment, calling on corporate leaders to demonstrate greater responsibility for job creation and wage growth. The Prime Minister cautioned businesses against relying solely on India's large consumer base, arguing that domestic demand should not discourage companies from pursuing higher standards or export opportunities. He also invited business leaders to openly share suggestions on reforms needed to accelerate the country's growth, stating: "Write to me openly. " The corporate tax reduction cited by PM Modi was introduced in September 2019 through the Taxation Laws Amendment Ordinance, now seven years ago. The Prime Minister also emphasised that India remained the world's fastest-growing major economy, with leading institutions projecting growth of around seven per cent. His message was clear: government concessions must be matched by greater corporate responsibility, particularly in creating jobs, raising wages and strengthening India's productive capacity. Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB India's first dedicated Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior gained significant momentum as 25 companies received Letters of Intent for land allotment at a ceremony in Bhopal yesterday (19 November). The first phase of the project secured investment commitments worth approximately Rs 3,600 crore and is expected to generate 15,600 jobs, Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia confirmed. The ceremony, attended by Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, also marked the announcement of Phase-II of the project, signalling an expansion of the zone's manufacturing ecosystem. The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet on Wednesday allocated another 450 acres for the zone to accommodate six companies, adding to the 170 acres already provided for the first phase. Scindia estimated overall employment from the project at around 18,000 positions. The Madhya Pradesh state cabinet had approved 170 acres for the country's first dedicated telecom manufacturing zone, which is envisaged as an integrated industrial cluster dedicated to telecom manufacturing, research and development, and innovation. The zone will accommodate manufacturers of telecom equipment, components, optical fibre, software and passive infrastructure. Earlier investor outreach programmes in New Delhi and Mumbai had secured investment commitments worth Rs 5,500 crore, with the potential to generate nearly 20,000 jobs. The project forms part of the Centre's efforts to strengthen domestic telecom supply chains and reduce dependence on imported equipment under the Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiatives. The Department of Telecommunications and the Madhya Pradesh government signed an agreement in July to establish the zone, with Madhya Pradesh holding a 51 per cent stake in the entity, while the Department of Telecommunications holds the remaining 49 per cent. The initiative aims to position India as a trusted global destination for telecom manufacturing. national_raw_news.title: LG Sinha vows action against terror ecosystem, assures support to slain SPOs' families
national_raw_news.content: LG Sinha vows action against terror ecosystem, assures support to slain SPOs’ families – Kashmir Dot Com Contact Us About Advertise Careers Home Kashmir Jammu World Politics Opinion Business Health Contact Us No Result View All Result Home Kashmir Jammu World Politics Opinion Business Health Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home JAMMU LG Sinha vows action against terror ecosystem, assures support to slain SPOs’ families by Kashmir Dot Com November 19, 2026 in JAMMU 0 0 SHARES 16 VIEWS Share on Facebook JAMMU, NOVEMBER 19: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha met a public delegation from Kiyar in Dachhan, Kishtwar, at Lok Bhavan today. The Lieutenant Governor paid homage to J&K Police brave hearts, Shri Rashpal Kumar and Shri Babi Chand. He assured that the administration will extend all possible support to the families of the martyrs. The delegation was led by Member of Legislative Assembly from Kishtwar Shagun Parihar. The delegation apprised the Lieutenant Governor of key issues pertaining to the prevailing security situation in Kiyar and other areas of Dachhan, Kishtwar. She also highlighted the concerns of residents living in remote and vulnerable pockets of Dachhan. The Lieutenant Governor reaffirmed an unwavering commitment to dismantling the terror ecosystem through decisive action. He reiterated the commitment to provide compensation, government employment, and comprehensive support to the Next of Kins of the Special Police Officers (SPOs), who laid down their lives in the line of duty. Addressing local priorities in Kiyar, the Lieutenant Governor assured of installation of a mobile tower in the area and committed to pursuing forest clearance for the Kiyar road with the relevant authorities. On establishing a Special Operations Group (SOG) picket, he said the issue will be discussed in the review meeting with Deputy Commissioners and Senior Superintendents of Police, scheduled for Friday. “The security grid, along with road and communication infrastructure in Kiyar and adjoining remote areas, will be strengthened for the safety and well-being of the local residents,” he said. The Lieutenant Governor assured the delegation that all other demands and grievances raised during the meeting would be addressed on priority. The delegation consisted of residents from Kiyar including Shri Suresh Kumar, Shri Pradeep Kumar, Shri Ram Lal Thakur, Shri Roshan Lal Thakur, Shri Satish Kumar Parihar, Shri Rohit Parihar. They were accompanied by District President, BJP Kishtwar, Ravi Parihar, from Lopara Dachhan; BJP District Vice President Kishtwar, Ashish Sharma from Berabhata, Lokesh Parihar from Suid, Dachhan and J&K BJP Mahila Morcha General Secretary Urvashi Gupta.
